utterances.text: Can we take that to be the case for the totality of your report, that there are occasions -- in fact, I would suggest to you that it's almost the rule in the course of this particular report that you have seldom actually weighed in behind the documents that you have -- or the accounts that you have described and said, "I conclude that this is true"; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct to state that do I as a rule, and this is true generally speaking as an analyst, not perceive it as my role to come in and say whether something is true or not. If I'm able to find documents that disagree with each other then I try to show that those persons disagreed about a particular event and characterised it in different ways. I refer to a number of those conflicts which are characterised power struggles, for example, characterised differently by various actors, but I'm highly aware again particularly in light of the sparse nature of the documentation that I've been able to examine that this is a small portion of the overall evidence and particularly because of the bad state of documentation, much of this chapter of the former Yugoslavia's history will need to be reconstructed based on witness statements which of course have their on methodological problems and biases.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And would you in fact agree that Arkan was a convenient, if I can use this expression, whipping horse for individuals who wanted to discredit others? A good way to do it would be to associate them with Arkan. Would that be an observation that you would agree with based on your review of the documentation and your understanding of the motives behind some of those documents?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot exclude that at times some persons have used Arkan, to use your term, as a whipping horse in order to discredit others. However, I would point out that for the bulk of the period under examination here, the vast majority of the actors in Serb-controlled entities in Krajina often had very positive opinions of Arkan and therefore were not using him as a whipping horse but in many cases were themselves rushing to associate themselves with him as a patriotic actor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: One aspect of this that I find interesting and I'm not sure what your views are on it is you've testified that you have reviewed evidence that Arkan was affiliated or under the authority of or controlled in some way by the DB of Serbia while at the same time you rely on DB reports making various assertions about his criminal conduct. Can you help shed some light on how you view the dynamic between on the one hand he is a part of the DB and on the other hand there are elements of the DB that are attempting to apparently discredit him or associate him with criminal activity?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you for that excellent question. I think this is one of the more fascinating aspects of the collapse of the former Yugoslavia. When we look at the police, and this is true. I want to make it very clear, not just in Serb-controlled entities but in the Bosnian Muslim portions of the police, in the Croatian controlled portion of the police that there is a protracted struggle going on in the police between a large section of the police who are professionally trained, who grew up in Yugoslavia, who were proud of the fact that they had been implementing the constitutional laws of Yugoslavia throughout their careers and upheld law and order, and the large influx of nationalist police officers and personnel that took place at the end of the 1980s and the beginning of 1990, and it is abundantly clear even in the sparse available documentation that this is the case in Eastern Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem as well. It was the case in Vojvodina. And many career police officers, both in the public security service and the State Security Service, were very resentful and looked very disapprovingly at the actions of people such as Arkan. I provide actually a number of documents from as far back as the 1980s where it was known that Arkan was a career criminal and therefore we need to remember that the police and even the vondit [phoen] State Security Service of Serbia is not a monolith. There are people, operational officers who had worked for years and who had covered Serbian extremism in their -- in the ambit of their work in, for example, Novi Sad, and these are the people who authored the types of reports that we see. So even though they are actually subordinate legally to the persons at the top of the MUP who are making use for Arkan and similar persons and providing them with the assistance they need, these persons are instinctively and professionally bound to file the types of reports that they file here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: That may be one explanation but I have another possible explanation that I would like to hear your comment upon, and that is: Do you think there is any possibility that some of these sources are in effect trying to for one motivation or another disavow the connection of these institutions of which they are part with the individual in question? In other words, are they by virtue of these creating a paper record to say, We have nothing to do with this particular individual, with Arkan?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot exclude that possibility, but in the -- particularly in the case of the correspondence from, for example, the state security centres in places like Sremska Mitrovica, Ruma, Novi Sad, one certainly does not gain the perspective or conclusion from examining those documents that that is the primary motivation for writing such reports. And I would also note that these reports are almost all classified at a very high level, which means that whatever disavowal they might have been engaged in would have been available to only very few select readers.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And what about reports by -- and you had addressed this in your testimony yesterday to some extent but you haven't gone into detail, what about reports by JNA -- various JNA sources in respect of Arkan?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, the question is whether or not there would be -- let's start with this question: Is there the same element of some would welcome Arkan and others would -- who are from a more professional background might wish to discredit or be open about discussing his activities?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's a relatively fair characterisation, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: We're going to come back to some documents in particular, but I just wanted to address those questions with you now as a matter of general methodology. And on that subject, you did testify yesterday and now that you have reviewed some testimony in this case and that you did consider it to be relevant but that nevertheless you haven't changed any aspect of your report. Can you explain what that means? Why did you choose not to change any aspect of your report based upon testimony that you considered relevant?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can tell the Court that when I was first -- when it was first suggested to me in December that I be permitted to examine the testimony and the witness statements of a small number of protected witnesses, my initial reaction, and it is still my reaction today is, Well, okay, I will do that if the Office of the Prosecutor thinks it is useful and if the Chamber permits it, but I as an analyst and as the author of this report am not certain what I am actually supposed to do that with that knowledge. And what I mean by that is because, number one, in accordance with the methodology that I've explained, even if I had read it a year ago, I could not have cited it. Number two, I cannot -- and again, as I am always fond of pointing out I'm not a lawyer. I know that I cannot legally be the vehicle for introducing those persons' testimony into this court. This is why they are called as witnesses. So, yes, my knowledge of the subject matter has been expanded, and as an analyst and historian that is always interesting and of course I could see that their evidence was germane and relevant to subjects I discussed in my report but I cannot see how I can go in and amend my report, and I do not see it as my role to comment on the veracity of what the witnesses say; that is for the Court to decide.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Did you think that you had -- let's say that you had considered that you did wish to change your report, did you believe, were you told that you would be able to make such amendments?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As soon as I raised the epistemological point that I just raised, it was a moot point. I mean, there was -- I -- I effectively said that I will not change my report, and said that before reading the statements because of the methodological considerations that went into drafting the report in the first place. If I opened that door, then logically I should be reading a whole lot more witness statements and suspect statements and availing myself of those.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But has the testimony that you have read affected your answers during your direct examination?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And again, I would like to make it clear that there are certain things that I could say now regarding certain paragraphs in my report, I'm not going to say which ones because we're in open session and I am aware that this is closed-session testimony that we are talking of here, there are certain paragraphs in this report in which certain very detailed events took place where I had a part of the puzzle. I was now made aware of a larger part of that puzzle because I read that testimony. But to answer your question, what could I have said? My answer would have been and I'm also aware that a certain person testified and this was actually not so. Again my assumption as an analyst is that the Court has now become aware of these person's company and they will take that into consideration when they weigh that testimony compared to the documents in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And you'd agree that in respect of some events that are contained in documents that you have relied on in your report in order to come to certain conclusions, to the extent that it turns out that those events didn't occur or have been misconstrued or not described in the right way, that would have an impact on the conclusions, the overall conclusions in your report; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I find your question somewhat mystifying because I just thought we just agreed there were very few conclusions in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, to the extent that there are any conclusions, would you agree that to the extent that they're the factual foundation as presented in the documents turns out to be substantially contradicted by reliable testimonial evidence that those conclusions are infirm.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the extent that that is the case, and I do believe that that is the case based on my review of that witness testimony, then I am fully confident that a panel of professional international Judges will be able to weight the evidence as is their task and see the totality of the picture of which I can only provide a small part.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 03221, which is Defence tab 4. Now, Dr. Nielsen, I'd like to discuss with you a couple of documents that we've received from the Office of the Prosecutor related to -- well, actually, I don't want to characterise what they're related to. I want to find out from you, actually, what they're -- what they're related to and what they mean. And this document appears to be an e-mail from you to various attorneys of the Office of the Prosecutor. Am I right in understanding that -- well, first of all have you seen this document recently?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw this document most recently when I believe that it was filed in the Karadzic case. And, yes, it is an e-mail I wrote.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And you were an employee of the Office of the Prosecutor when you wrote this e-mail?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I think just because this is going to become very relevant in a second, let's get the exact dates of my employment at the OTP. I was employed from mid-June 2002 until the middle of August 2004. That was the first stint at the employment -- at the OTP for me. And my second stint was from the 14th of February, 2006, until the 31st of December of 2007. So this was written during my second period of employment with the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And if we could turn to page 2 down at the bottom there is a reference to -- by you. There is a reference to the current draft. Just before we get into the substance, what -- what is the current draft that you're referring to? Current draft of what?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was referring in this e-mail to the current draft of a proposed expert report, Prosecution expert report that was being prepared for the case of Stanisic and Simatovic, a report that I had initially started drafting in -- during my first period of employment at the Tribunal and which upon the termination of my employment when I went to the ICC, I had relinquished control of that report, and upon my return to the Tribunal in 2006 there was a discussion of the extent to which I would be involved again in drafting the version of that report that went into court or that would be filed before the Court, keeping in mind that during my second stint of my employment at the OTP I was no longer working as a full-time analyst for the leadership research team but was addressing other matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] And what you say down here in the last sentence --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And what you say in the last sentence of this e-mail is: "However, given that the current draft cites verbatim some passages of Ari's report," and above you've referred to Ari as Ari Kerkkanen who appears to be another analyst, and then you go on, "passages of Ari's report without Ari ever being mentioned I want to raise this possible issue." Am I right in understanding that the concern that you're raising here is that there is a report that is going to be submitted under your name that contains work by another analyst who is not identified as one of the authors of the report?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you precisely what's going on here. Ari Kerkkanen was an analyst who did not work for the leadership research team but who worked for another team at the Office of the Prosecutor, and he had been for a long time been one of the analysts who had been focusing most of his time and effort on the RSK. He was one of the analysts who was also involved in those document collection missions that took place earlier. He had written and filed an expert report in the Martic case, I believe it was, and after he had testified in the Martic case, I believe at some point in 2005 he had left the Tribunal, and he had made it known that he would not be interested in testifying on the basis of that report in any other cases. He had been asked whether he would be interested in testifying again and he said no. So it was to the degree there would be other cases in which the -- that would deal with the RSK MUP which analysts and which analytical products would deal with that and that is part of the discussion that we have here. What I was trying to highlight, first of all, was the fact that as we can see on this page, the Trial Chamber in Martic essentially discarded Mr. Kerkkanen's report. The other thing I was trying to highlight was that I was probing whether the material that was used in his report was -- to what extent that was going to be used in any future analytical reports that the leadership research team might file, and I want to make reference to page -- I believe it's 13199 [sic] of the Karadzic transcript in which you will find a detailed discussion by Dr. Patrick Treanor, who was the leader of the leadership research team, in which he outlined the methodology used by the leadership research team which, among other things, produced a number of reports where, for example, it was Dr. Treanor's name alone that appeared on the first page, but several unnamed analysts who were also on the leadership research team had written entire sections of that report and although their names did not appear in the report. So this is what I'm trying to find out. Is that what we're doing here or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] And thank you very much for that transcript reference. It's not --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that transcript reference. It's not often that one has a witness providing such references, so I appreciate it very much.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It should be page "13999." It says "13199" here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And you received a response saying, Thanks, I have seen that passage from the -- from the attorney to whom you've written and what do you propose in terms of your report, and then your answer is, I'm not proposing anything in particular because I am not myself sure to what extent, if any, this will affect the overall report and the testimony about it. Can I first ask you how much of the report at this stage had actually been authored by Mr. Kerkkanen?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we're now going back to a particular point in time -- I believe my e-mail's from 2007, so we're talking about something that occurred six years ago. I'm not sure at that exact point in time what had -- how much of the report had come into existence and how much of the material he had used or written had been appropriated for the new report. What I can say is that I do recall in -- from my own documentation that it was only later that year that I was able to sit down and review the entire report as it was being filed, again because I was working on other issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 03231. It's related to Defence tab 1, even though it is not actually the number given at tab 1. I sent an e-mail at 7.58 this morning. I don't know whether there's an objection from the Prosecution or not on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I didn't want to raise earlier because Dr. Nielsen is perfectly capable of answering these questions; however, we're now getting into issues relating to reports written in a different case about totally different matters, and I'm not sure I understand what is the relevance of these questions in relation to a report prepared in this case from scratch with totally different material. If there is an issue with which the Defence want to impeach the witness, if there's a credibility issue, they should get to it directly. All these background e-mails and matters related to a different case on different topics, again I'm not entirely sure what is relevant. As I say, Dr. Nielsen is capable of answering these questions. I'm not sure if we've laid down the foundation or there's any relevance in it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: The relevance is to determine whether or not Dr. Nielsen lent his name to a report that he had not authored and that affects his credibility. Now in no way, I want to make very clear, am I making that insinuation at this stage. But in the absence of a statement from the witness that explains to me the situation which has been indicated by documents from the Office of the Prosecutor that leaves many unanswered questions, I would be derelict in my duty if I did not explore these questions with him. They are perfectly relevant to his expertise and the manner in which he has conducted himself as an expert at this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And are you saying, Mr. Gosnell, that you wouldn't ask the question directly to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, I to some degree need to lay a foundation as to what we're talking about because it's a fairly specific point, and I'm sorry if it's laborious for the Prosecution and I'm sorry in they're embarrassed by it, but, nevertheless, that's the process that I would suggest needs to be gone through to get to the right questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, if that is the reason why my learned friend wishes to use the report now that we have an explanation, I don't have any objection. And again, there is no issue of embarrassment. These are matters that have been disclosed to the Defence, so I don't think we need to take it that far.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Just to insist, I don't plan to go in any way into the content of the report. All I wish to do is to show the witness the cover page and the table of contents, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Just a small correction to the transcript. At line 22, I said these are matters that were "disclosed" to the Defence not "closed."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Gosnell, but you could perhaps speed up a little bit to the very purpose of your -- to come to the very purpose of your line of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I'll try to do that, Mr. President, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, Dr. Nielsen, is it correct that this is the submitted version of the report that in June 2007 you referred to as being a draft version?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's certainly the title page. There were several drafts of the report, so -- but I'm assuming if this is the ERN version, it was the version filed in Stanisic and Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 03221, please. I'm sorry, I've given the wrong number. It's 03231, Defence tab 1. Sorry, could we go back to 03212. Sorry, that doesn't appear to be the document I'm looking for. The correct number should be 03232, and I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now -- now, this -- just to describe this, I mean, this is -- this is dated 14th of September, 2009, and your name is there appearing as the author alone; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. While we're on this topic, let me just explain. When I prepared the original RS MUP report for Krajisnik, for the Krajisnik case, I had a brief section on the assistance received by RS MUP from federal and Serb authorities of internal affairs. Subsequently we of course received many more documents that cast light on that important subject. I therefore was encouraged during my first period of employment to take that addendum or portion of the original Krajisnik report and expand it into a full report on the involvement of the federal secretariat of internal affairs in Republic of Serbia Ministry of Internal Affairs in Bosnia-Herzegovina. That is part of what became the report we saw just a moment ago. And then now this is yet another addendum to the Stanisic and Simatovic report. In this case the addendum was authored by myself alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: All right. Can we now about to 03231, please. Now, this document, which is an earlier document, includes Ms. Tromp's name as one of the authors. Can you explain why she has been removed from the subsequent iteration of the report in the same case?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think if I looked at those two cover pages as I just saw them, the previous one and this one, it's not the -- it's not two iterations of the same report. It's a report and an addendum. So her name was not removed. She was just not involved in the production of the addendum.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: All right. Let's go straight then to 1D190, which really gets to the point. And if we go over to page 2 of this document, paragraph 5. Now, this document says that in the course of final preparations to call you, the Prosecution discovered that portions of the report -- or chapters, chapters 1 of the report were not authored by Christian Nielsen. Chapter 1 represents a composite of the work of two individuals. Chapter 3 represents a composite of the work of Ari Kerkkanen and Nena Tromp. Now, first of all, let me just stop there. Is it correct that the chapter 3 being referred to, that's the chapter that concerns Croatia and any Serb entities in Croatia; is that right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is clearly stated in the first sentence of this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Correct. Thank you for that. And then the last sentence says: As such Mr. Nielsen will be unable to properly address challenges or answer questions regarding chapters 1 to 3 of the report. Now, why did you -- why did you tell them that on the one hand, that you would not be able to answer challenges to that portion of the report, whereas the previous document that we've seen lists your name and your name alone as the author of the report to be submitted in that case?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think here again to use the old expression mixing, you know, apples and pears or apples and oranges, there is a distinction to my mind between a report on the cover of which two names appear, my name and the name of Nena Tromp. And as far as I know, all iterations of that report that were filed in Stanisic and Simatovic have both names on the cover page. Then there was an addendum, and I was the sole author of the addendum produced as I recall, mainly based on more recent material produced or given to the OTP by the State Security Services of Serbia who were hardly forthcoming in their provision of relevant documentation hence the late arrival of documentation that was relevant and needed to be reviewed and which became the subject of that addendum. So to go back to your question, I did not tell them, if them is the Prosecution, what you say -- say that I told them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you for that correction, but your name and Ms. Tromp's name do appear on the main report as submitted on the 18th of March, 2008, as the authors. Now, wouldn't that imply that at least as of the date of submission of that report the proposition was that you would be in a position, either you or Ms. Tromp or both, would be in a position to vouch for and respond to questions concerning the content of that report?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the position as of the day of the filing of that report, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And then did you subsequently object? How is it -- well, let me just ask you: Did you subsequently object?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not subsequently object, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Would you have been willing to testify and answer questions in relation to that report in the Stanisic and Simatovic case?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think here we need to make a distinction between the two issues referred to in paragraph 5 of this filing. One is this chapter 3 which is, as noted, represented a composite of the work of the Ari Kerkkanen and Nena Tromp. As I noted, there had been a practice within the OTP that on some occasions one analyst would in court present the conclusions or analytical observations of several OTP analysts. So pursuant to that practice, I did not have a problem with presenting that portion of the report. The understanding, of course, both by myself and by the Prosecutors was that I would in detail go through all portions of that report, review all of the documentation, read all the primary source of the documentation and make myself capable of responding to questions that any party to the case would have. So there those -- that's how I would respond to that part of the concern. With chapter 1, there is, to my mind, a completely different and much more serious problem, which is that chapter 1 as is stated here, and I quote, "Represents a composite of the work of Budimir Babovic and Nena Tromp." Budimir Babovic was at no point an employee of the Office of the Prosecutor, and I would at no point have agreed had I known that -- that portions of his work had been directly integrated into that report. I would at no point have agreed to testify on the basis of that. That to me was a clear violation of the procedures that we had established.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And you say that even if you had done what you just said you would do in respect of these reports, namely review all the primary material yourself, essentially make it your own. Are you saying that even if you had done that, the fact that someone else, a non-employees had been involved in the preparation of the report, are you saying that you still would not have been willing to testify in respect of such a report?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I believe I provided a clear answer in terms of chapter 3, the composite work produced based on the work of Ari Kerkkanen and Nena Tromp, again because those persons were both employees of the Office of the Prosecutor. My objection was to chapter 1 which represented a composite of the work of an external expert which to my mind the Prosecution, the Defence, and anyone else is perfectly welcome to call external experts but then they should be testifying on the basis of their reports. And Prosecution, members of the Prosecution, including analysts in the Office of the Prosecutor should not be presenting the work of external experts as their own and I would never have agreed to testify on the basis of that section of the report given that it was produced based on at least in part analysis done by Mr. Babovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And just to close this topic, could we have Defence tab 3, 65 ter 03220. Now you've just told us that your objection to testifying on the basis of that report was the involvement of an external expert so to speak. What we have here is a memorandum disclosed by the Prosecution dated the 28th of March, 2011, and according to this memorandum, you expressed shock when told that portion of the report were Babovic's and Kerkkanen's work. The reason why I'm really focusing on this is because Mr. Kerkkanen is the one who prepared, as I understand it, the portion of the report on the RSK and Croatia; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, and I think, you know, this is a historic opportunity for me to be able to comment on hearsay about my own role, because this to me is hearsay. And so here I am as a witness, and what I can tell you is it makes absolutely zero sense to say that I expressed shock when told that portions of the report were Kerkkanen's work. Why would I express shock in 2011 when as we have seen in my e-mail, and I'm very glad you produced that, in 2007 I was cognisant of the fact that parts of Kerkkanen's work were being appropriated for a joint analytical report. To me that was part and parcel of an agreed OTP methodology in the leadership research team when we had several OTP analysts. Instead of walking three analysts into the report -- to the court on one report, sometimes we would have three or four analysts but one witnessing, one testifying analyst who would position himself or herself to testify on the basis of that entire report. So my shock which was present, and I can tell you I was apoplectic when I received this phone call, referred or pertained exclusively to the knowledge that I obtained on that day, that portions of the report were Babovic's work. To me that was as I stated a clear and absolutely unacceptable violation of the standards that I had tried to uphold in producing analytical work and I can tell you that speaking personally, professionally as an analyst, that is the one reason that I have drawn a very clear conclusion and that is that I will never again produce any joint analytical research report that is going into a court case, and that is why I said if I'm going to do a report for the Hadzic case, I will draft it from scratch solely based on my own analysis and my own review of documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I wish to interrupt my learned friend. I've been just informed carefully that this document has a restriction. Could we make sure we don't display it? I mean the testimony itself -- is it not restricted?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document was not broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So is it -- is it wrong and substantively this is important for questions I might ask you later on, are you -- well, what is your view of the quality of the portion of the expert report in the Stanisic case concerning Croatia?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not re-read recently that portion of the expert report. I haven't looked at it since it was withdrawn as we can see that some time ago. But what I recalled at the time was that it contained a significant number of what I thought were pertinent and potentially relevant points about the operation of the RSK MUP, although the focus there to be clear in that report was not so much on the RSK MUP itself as on the assistance that the RSK MUP had received from Serbia or from the federal Yugoslav authorities and their presence on the territory of the RSK. But to make any more detailed statement about the quality of that portion of the report I would have to revisit it. I want to state again very clearly for the record that that report was not used to draft this report and that this report that we have in front of us today is drafted from scratch starting in January 2012, and therefore to me is an entirely different analytical product, particularly because I wanted to absolutely avoid even the merest association of such problems as the ones we've seen here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, I appreciate that answer, sir, and we can remove this document. Now, I'd like to move to a new topic and I'd like to plunge into the substance of your report, if I may, and I'd like to start by looking at some of the large number of JNA documents that you -- some of which you have been shown by the Prosecution and others you have not seen but that are either referred to -- referred to in your proofing note or in your report. But just to ask as a general matter in respect of these documents, am I correct in understanding that in a context where there are few police documents from the SBWS, these documents provide a valuable insight by reflection or indirectly as to what may have been going on amongst police entities in the region?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, and I would point out that precisely when one as an analyst encounters such documentation, it's sometimes not clear where to draw the line between whether that documentation should be more appropriately cited in a report on the police or more appropriately cited in a report on the military since those organs have many joint operations and joint dealings. But in a number of cases where there were clear references to the police, I thought them sufficiently relevant to include in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, let's start going through them. Could we have P365, Prosecution tab 337. For the very first -- this document is from the command of the 12th Corps, Chief of Staff Colonel Srboljub Trajkovic, to the command of the 1st Military District. Now, what's your understanding of the territorial location or scope of the 12th Corps at this stage which is the 8th of November, 1981?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not have a well developed understanding of the operational area or area of responsibility of the corps at that particular point in time and I would refer -- or, defer on that and similar questions to the military expert as the sole reason I would look at such documents and I see this is one of the more recent arrivals was to see what it said about the police stations which are among the things mentioned in this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And we see in the very first two sentences a reference to an order that was issued on the 16th of October, 1991, by the 1st Military District. Now, I've asked you about the 12th Corps. Do you know what the geographic scope or extent was of the jurisdiction of the 1st Military District?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I would reiterate my response to the previous question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And this order, according to this report, says the order lists the related tasks of local commands, i.e., formation of civilian authority organs with the citizens, compilation of lists of military conscripts, functioning of services needed for the life and work of citizens so that law and order can be establish by the time the police force is formed. Would you agree with me that that seems to imply that at least as of this date there doesn't seem to be any police force present as far as the JNA is concerned at the date that order is given?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with that and that is something we discussed earlier and I note that later in the same document they talk about how to enable the formation of, as they call it, legal police stations.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that as of the date of this report anyway, which is the 8th of November, 1991, there is doubt in the minds of the commander of the 12th Corps about whether he should be co-operating with any element of the SBWS civilian government?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and that ties into some of my testimony yesterday where I spoke about the fact that the military seems uncertain about the legality of the authorities of this area, including the legality of any police station that they might have formed, and that's the gist of the paragraph further down. It's the first, second, third -- fourth paragraph on the -- in the B/C/S original.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: If we turn to page 2 of the English --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell, would this be an appropriate moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: This would be a very appropriate moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Dr. Nielsen, second break. We'll come back at 12.45. You will be escorted out. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Dr. Nielsen, would you agree with me that the reference here to the formation of civilian authority organs with the citizens in your experience of the use of that terminology would also imply formation of the police?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I would just note that the reference I was pointing to in the B/C/S version is actually in the fifth paragraph in the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that. And would you agree that the reference here to formation of civilian authority organs with the citizens as well as the other tasks that are prescribed because here this refers to tasks, would you agree with me that this appears to set out a fairly comprehensive agenda for what perhaps could be described as civilian reconstruction?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, I don't believe that we have actually seen the original order of the 16th of October, 1991, and I know that this will be a very difficult question for you. Do you have any recollection whether you saw that original order from the 16th of October, 1991, as part of your research?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not have a recollection of seeing the original order. If that original order has been obtained, then it most likely would have arrived with this most recent batch of documents from the military archives of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that it's particularly significant the author's puzzlement about how to deal with the local civilian authorities, in particular of the district of the SBWS, given that he is writing from Dalj, which at this time is or is near the seat of that government?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I would state that I think the author's puzzlement, because it is a similar puzzlement that I have seen in other documents from this period, has nothing to do with geographical proximity but rather with the lack of clarity as to whether these self-proclaimed Serb autonomous districts have legal force or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, I guess what I'm saying is if there's one place you would expect the organs of the district government to exist and be visible to someone such as the author of this report, it would be there, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: And as I read the document, the author of the document is observing such organs to some extent. They're not fully operational, many of them, but even to the extent that they do exist, including in Dalj, he is not clear about what degree of legal legitimacy they have.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And if we look at page 2 of the English, I believe it would still be page 1 of the B/C/S, in any event, it's the third last paragraph, this author recommends co-operating with the Assembly and the government of the district of SBWS, and what I find significant here is the law that's being invoked by the author. He says to establish and develop authority together with them and by applying the laws of the SFRY and the Republic of Serbia which they accepted as their own. Do you consider that significant, or what do you make of that particular reference?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do consider that significant, and as I believe I may have stated yesterday, I think that is an important reflection of the desire of -- often-declared desire of the particular district, the Serb autonomous district, the SAO Krajina and other Serb entities in Croatia to remain bound by the legislation of the SFRY and the Republic of Serbia and to some extent it is reflective also of their ultimate aspirations to join in a greater political unity with those areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And this author draws a distinction between his recommendation that there should be co-operation with the organs of the SBWS government and the Territorial Defence. Here he says in the last -- the third last and the second last paragraph, in the third last paragraph he says, Yes, let's recognise and co-operate with the government, and then in the second last paragraph he says, But the TO should be disbanded. Do you agree that that's what the document says?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. And I note that he would also very much like Arkan to leave as well as other paramilitary formations like Arkan's.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And what if anything does this distinction in his own recommendation between the government and the TO, at least as it exists in Dalj, what does that tell you, if anything, about the relationship between the government and the TO in Dalj?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, speaking solely based on the document that we have in front of us, there seems to be at some level even a potential contradiction, because while he, on one hand, Colonel Trajkovic is stating that he regards the Assembly and the government of the -- of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem as a legitimate representative of authority and one that was elected by the Serbian people, he on the other hand seems to not be very fond of the Territorial Defence formed by that same group of people. Now, as to whether his grounds for that are based in military or other law, that would be -- I could only speculate.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But would you agree at least that this seems to suggest that in the mind of this author there is a substantial difference in the identity of these two institutions, on the one hand the TO Dalj, and on the other hand the district government?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, with the caveat again that it seems that one, that is the Territorial Defence, has been formed by the other. In fact, he also asks -- he says, To which extent should we recognise the Territorial Defence of the SAO Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem which is connected to the government. So he sees them as being linked.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, I don't have the benefit of the original, but in the English you'll note that -- you'll see there's the use of the passive tense, and what it says there is that the Territorial Defence has been formed in the SBWS SO. It doesn't say, at least not as it's translated in English, it doesn't say that the district government has formed that TO.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are correct in saying that -- the language states that as it has been formed in the Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem SO, but I would again point out that earlier on the same page we have that question which denotes Trajkovic's understanding that the Territorial Defence of the Serb district of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem is linked to the government, or as it's translated in English here in the official translation, "which is connected to the government."

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And where is that reference?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the English version which we have in front of us on the screen here, it's the second paragraph on the page: "To what extent should we recognise the Territorial Defence of the Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem SO, which is connected to the government?"

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But then in the last paragraph at least he doesn't repeat that there's that particular connection, does he?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct characterisation of the document that he does not repeat that assertion.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And of course he doesn't elaborate on what he means when he says connected, does he?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in this particular document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And since you're not a military expert, I'm not going to get into the niceties of the status of the TO at this time, but I simply wanted to explore the issue of his distinction in terms of what he considered to be the level of co-operation with the two entities. Could we now have Prosecution tab 338, which is 65 ter 06026. Now, this document appears to be from the command of the 1st Military District to the 12th Corps and the 1st Guards Brigade, and in the preamble it says there that: "The federal secretariat of defence is drafting instructions for the establishing tasks, and competencies of military authorities in liberated places." Do you recall whether you've ever seen that document, the instructions in question that are referred to there?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe this is one of the documents I had a chance to review, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And this document appears to say that pending the promulgation of those instructions, this order is being promulgated, and I'm particularly interested in the third bullet item under item 2 where it says: "Establish civilian authorities, take steps to establish law and order, safety of citizens, basic supply functions and other communal needs." Now, again, do you see that this reflects the JNA's assumption of very significant civilian tasks in the area?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, though unfortunately the translation once again does not reflect the B/C/S original fully, because what it actually says is "until the establishment of civilian authorities take these steps." So I think that's an important thing there. Again that confirms what we've been discussing, that they are saying we have to do certain things until those civilian authorities can be established in these areas and they are desirous of those civilian authorities coming into existence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But in the meantime, the concept is that the JNA is going to assume the authority of a government in the area; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they certainly abhor a vacuum, and they are trying to -- well aware as we know from other documents of the type of behaviour that is rampant in this area establish some modicum of order.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, over the page in English at point 5, the author of this report, and again this is a report of the 20th of November, 1991, indicates that the organs of authority in the SO SBWS and the municipalities with the exception of Beli Manastir are still undeveloped. Now, do you agree with me here that there appears to be the introduction of some kind of distinction between the district government of SBWS and the municipalities? We'll get into it further, but do you see that that distinction is being drawn by the author?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a distinction between the district level authorities and the constituent municipalities within that district.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And it says they mostly have only individuals responsible for certain departments or a single commissioner for the municipality or locality. This causes problems and delays in their engagement. Are you aware of the position of a commissioner of a municipality?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am to some extent aware of that position, and what I mean by that is I've seen that term used in several of the documents that I've reviewed. I'm more familiar with the way it was used in the case of Bosnia and Herzegovina, but often commissioners were established in the short term after the "liberation" of certain municipalities, or in cases where there were the municipality, for example, was threatened by renewed warfare.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And it says in the last sentence: "The local commands should be show patience in resolving problems, but also persist in their co-ordinating role of bringing together all subjects to ensure that problems are effectively resolved." Now, the word "co-ordination" is a term of art in military lexicon, and I don't propose to go into that with you, but do you see here that this as it's used here in this sentence that the JNA is essentially saying to itself, We need to knock heads together in order to set up this institution?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may, again as I do as an analyst rely on the B/C/S original, I would point out that the B/C/S original to my mind is much more correctly translated as "in its capacity as a co-ordinator," rather than in their co-ordinating role. So in their capacity as a co-ordinator, they are supposed to bring together all these subjects to ensure that the problems are effectively resolved, so, yes, this means this is a joint effort and all hands on deck and we need to establish appropriate civilian authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And -- and the interlocutor, so to speak, that's being referred to in this paragraph, and we'll come to paragraph 6 in a moment, but the interlocutor being dealt with, the actors being referred to, these are municipal authorities as you read it; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what's being discussed here, although again from the greater sum of documentation, the -- in the hierarchy of the district, the district authorities also have a role to play and they are mentioned in other documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, it's mentioned in the very next paragraph, in fact. And here it says that co-operation with the government of both the Republic of Serbia and the SO of SBWS will be ensured by the 1st Military District with municipal organs by local commands in whose zones of responsibility they lie. So do you see here that a distinction is being drawn? On the one hand the 1st Military District is going to discuss or resolve issues with the Republic of Serbia and with the district government, whereas the town commands or the commands that are on the ground are primarily to co-ordinate with municipalities?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Then there's a -- the last sentence in that context is interesting and I'd like to know what -- how -- what you make of it. The command of the 12th Corps and the 1st Proletarian Guards Mechanised Brigade and the Vukovar garrison command shall co-operate with the government of the SO SBWS to the extent necessary to resolve problems in their zones of responsibility? How would you interpret that last -- and you have the benefit of reading the original. How would you interpret the meaning of that last sentence?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, we have to see this type of correspondence. It's obviously part of a larger record of correspondence. I think we are all aware of the types of problems they were facing and this is again one of those reminders, if you will, that the relevant organs, both military and civilian, at various levels, municipal, district, et cetera, and as we see including even authorities from Serbia as needed, should get involved in order to address these problems as soon as possible. So that is what I read this document as saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But do you read that sentence to mean only co-operate no more than necessary, or do you take it to mean actively co-operate with the government to achieve certain ends?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says to the extent necessary, and that's an accurate translation of the B/C/S original, and I would just leave it at that, because I think drawing either conclusion that you suggest in your question is not possible based merely on this language.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But you'd agree that either reading is possible at least; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure, those are two possible readings of that sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And then down at the bottom it says that no organs of authority have yet been established or commissioners appointed for the municipalities of Osijek, Vinkovci, and Dalj. Does that correspond with what you know? Is it true that there were no either commissioners in those municipalities, nor that such municipalities had any other effective organs of government at that stage?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only again refer to my general awareness of the extreme contingency of the re-establishment or establishment of civilian organs. It would be a much more demanding analytical exercise, perhaps a productive one, to go in and try to establish based on the available documentation precisely on which date which municipalities had which organs coming into functioning but I have no reason to doubt the information that is provided by the officer who is the author of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Who is assigned to the 1st Military District based in Belgrade; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and who is -- such is my assumption based on other documents like this that I've reviewed. Obviously, there's a lot of detail here and he's receiving this information on a running basis from his subordinate units and trying to also construct as complete a picture as he can of what by all accounts is a very confusing situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: A very confusing situation in which perceptions therefore become all the more important and would you agree with me that this being a report from the 1st Military District, what we're seeing is the JNA's perception, that in the absence of other authorities it continues to assert whether by necessity or desire a fairly broad authority in respect of these areas; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perceptions are important to the extent that particularly -- I mean, unless a person is physically located in a given municipality or settlement, that person is obviously reliant upon these subjective conclusions of others who are reporting back to him that various authorities are or are not functioning. What you or I consider to be properly functioning authorities may not be in complete accordance and such might be here as well. I can only mention and I think it's relevant that I know from the greater totality of documentation that I've established that there were problems with some, particularly civilian officials, in Western Srem, Baranja, and Eastern Slavonia who allegedly on paper were performing these functions of civilian authority but who were in fact happily ensconced in their weekend cottages in Vojvodina instead all the while drawing salaries for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: The point being that -- the point I'm trying to make, sir, is that orders are being formulated in Belgrade based upon the perception reflected in this officer's document, saying as far as he's concerned there's no obstacle or impediment to the JNA exercising this needed authority in respect of the tasks identified; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I would assume that that is the way in which he has to formulate orders. He didn't have much alternative. As to how often this particular commander did or did not go to the field, I have no information about that. Again, as a point of logic and knowing military chain of command, my assumption is at the higher level way up here in Belgrade, he is to the best of his ability trying to make a picture of the situation based on reports from his subordinates and, perhaps if he had time, also by visiting the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 06031, which is Prosecution tab 339.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I apologise. I noticed that at the beginning my learned friend referred to the 65 ter number of this document which reminded me that it hasn't been tendered. Considering that we've been dealing with it in detail, perhaps this should be an appropriate time to tender it in evidence if my learned friend agrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you for that reminder. We would tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Demirdjian, did you deal with it in your examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I did, Your Honours, and I may have the reference. At page 2487.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit D19. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 06031, please. This is Prosecution tab 339.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: This document is from the command of the 80th Motorised Brigade. It says to the command. It doesn't specify further to whom. And it's dated the 22nd of November, 1991, and the content of the document refers to various events in Vukovar, and one of the aspects of this report is it says that there is an 80th Military Police Company being deployed or relocated to Vukovar barracks, and I'd suggest that that implies that there is a Military Police Company present in the area. Do you have any idea and I know you're not a military expert, but how many men are in a company usually in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know about company strengths in NATO forces to some extent, but I have no idea whether that in any way, shape, or form conform to the size of companies in the JNA. I would point out that what we have in front of me is the archival copy of an order that was issued by the command. So when it says in the B/C/S original "Command A/A," that is a typical example of an order that is being issued by a command, and of course they file an appropriate copy of that in their archives.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Item 2 says: "The Vukovar Territorial Defence Staff in co-operation with the command of the 80th Motorised Brigade will establish organs of authority in local communes and organise their functioning, set up police stations, regulate movements of the population returning to town and their compulsory identification at the Velepromet reception centre." Would you agree with me that for starters that this is an order being given from the JNA to what appears to be a TO unit?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Such it appears.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I should correct myself. It's not a TO unit. It's a TO staff, namely the Vukovar TO staff.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And we can continue to look at the entirety of the document. It goes over to page 2 in the English. Would you agree with me that there is no reference in this document at all to any organ of the SBWS, governmental organ of the SBWS?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And there's no suggestion whatsoever in this document that the JNA or at least the author considers that the JNA is in any way subordinated or under the control or authority of the SBWS government; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in this document. I would also note that I'm assuming that the preface to the document where the author refers the lieutenant-colonel to the newly established situation is referring to the quite recent end of armed conflict in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you this since you're appearing to express some hesitation on this issue: Was there anything in the previous two documents that we looked at that suggests to you that they -- that those organs considered themselves subordinated or under the control of or under the authority of the SBWS government?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not hesitating. I was just making sure I had read the document through before commenting on it, but, no, I have not seen in these three documents that we have now looked at information suggesting that these organs considered themselves subordinate to the SBWS government. There are, on the contrary, suggestions in some of the other documents that they at times would deem it necessary to co-operate with organs of those government -- of that government.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: For the record the two documents that Dr. Nielsen are referring to are P365 and D19. I'd now like to tender 06031.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit D20. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 06041, which is Prosecution tab 342.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now, this is from the 1st Proletarian Guards Brigade to the 1st Guards Division which of course would be the superior entity in the chain of command. And it's dated the 8th of December, 1991. And it appears to be signed by someone called Milorad Vujcic, who is a colonel and identifies himself as the commander. Now, this document says that with a view to establishing the situation in individual liberated places in the zone of responsibility of our unit, we submit the following information, and it says that civilian authorities have been established in the villages where there are residents, namely Negoslavci and the village of Petrovci, where they were elected by the local population. Now, is there any surprise there that these officials would have been elected by the local population?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the context of the armed conflict in both Croatia and in Bosnia-Herzegovina, it is my experience that when new organs of authority are established after hostilities have ceased, shortly after hostilities have ceased, then those authorities are often formed from below and not from above, and only at later points in time will the government organs that are legally superior to them take a position as to whether to, as it were, ratify those appointments or not. It's particularly in these cases where we see both in Eastern Slavonia, Baranja, and Srem and throughout Bosnia that we get a lot of these personality conflicts, because the top level does not always approve of the people who are appointed right after the end of the conflict at the local level.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And is there the same phenomenon within TO staffs?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is something that I cannot answer based on the information I have. It would not surprise me, but I cannot based on my own review of documents make that conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, that question does intersect at the issue of police forces for reasons that are going to become clear further in this document, but what we see in respect of the Territorial Defence Staff is that according to this author, they "exist in all populated localities, Petrovci, Negoslavci, Barack, Svinjarevci, and they were set up after the liberation and before the arrival of our unit to this area. The STO Territorial Defence staffs have their commanders and deputies as well as three to five members." The least that can be said here from this document is that there's no suggestion at all of any involvement by the district government of the SBWS in the formation of these TO staffs; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I stated in a number of places, the police stations were formed, as it were, organically based on whoever was left in that particular area or as we also see here in the third point of this document, in Negoslavci it's the formation of the police station is being done by the MUP of Serbia. So in many cases this is happening at the local level and not at the district level.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: All right. Well, you've anticipated my next question, which is the MUP does appear to be involved at least in respect of the police station of Negoslavci, the MUP of Serbia to be clear. Does that -- or can you help us understand how it is that personnel from the MUP of Serbia are entering into this territory and engaging in this task?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I refer at a couple of instances in my report to the fact that there had, for example, been meetings in the federal secretariat for internal affairs where one of the points of discussion was how to assist in the formation of police stations in these border areas, particularly the area of Croatia that was Eastern Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem. Similar discussions took place about some of the towns along the Drina River in Bosnia that are again also bordering Serbia where the MUP, either the federal MUP alone or in co-operation with the MUP of Serbia, played an active role in forming police stations during this period. And it should be said often also in the combat operations that led to these areas being put under Serb control. So when I see this type of document and the mention of a role by the republican MUP of Serbia in the formation of a police station in Negoslavci, this to me is -- it is highly likely that that is linked to these types of policies that had been decided in Belgrade. And again I would make reference - pardon me - to the working group, for example -- this is of a later date, but there are previous meetings like this in paragraph 173 of my report. I talk a bit later about the continued help that's being offered by Belgrade to get the MUP in the RSK up and running.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And on page 3 of the English it says: "Our brigade has set up village commands in keeping with the order of the division command. However, the real zone of responsibility does not correspond to the graphic representation attached to the order." So am I right in saying that this person is pointing out that there is some kind of a deviation from what would be expected, namely that the commander in the zone is the one responsible for setting up town commands in those towns in the zone; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, particularly in areas where armed hostilities had only recently ceased. The actual control of territory on the ground seems not to have corresponded to diagrams, charts, wish lists, or whatever we want to call them that had been composed at higher levels. This is also why we even see when they get around to talking about secretariats of internal affairs in Eastern Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem, we talked about and it's in the report that they would very much have liked to have had such a secretariat in Vinkovci. Vinkovci obviously was not under Serbian control so therefore they found a temporary location for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And, again, no indication here of any role by the district governments much less by the district government of the SBWS, much less that the district government is asserting authority or control over the JNA?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no such indication in this document. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I would tender that document now, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Just for the record, the document has already been MFI'd as P377 pending correction of the translation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So, Mr. Gosnell, no need to do anything for the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: No need. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have 06042, which is Prosecution tab 343.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: This document has a slightly nonuniform translation, but it does appear to be a single document, and it appears to be from the commander of the -- the 3rd Proletarian Guards Motorised Brigade command, commander Slobodan Antonic. It's dated 9th of December, 1991, from Tovarnik village. And over at page 2 we see that local communes have been "formed at the proposal and with the help of the town commands formed from units which were in these areas before us." Now, these again -- it should be clear, but these town commands are entities and organs of the JNA; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, as I believe I've stated now on at least two occasions, I'm not an expert on the issue of town commands or the JNA, so I would like to defer on whose creation those are to the military expert. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, there's no indication of any civilian role or involvement or any involvement of any organ at all of the SBWS in town commands, is there?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Though again I think this is a very interesting document because we are now in December 1991, and we see the kind of transition starting that I spoke of just a bit earlier, which is that even though they have not been formed at the local level with the involvement of the district authorities, now that we are ostensibly a little bit removed in time from outright armed conflict, the Assembly isn't -- and other authorities are increasingly coming to play a role and that's what I spoke of earlier where we now get this negotiation between whether these formations are allowed to continue to exist as they had been established with those personnel, or whether they needed to be changed in some way, shape, or form.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But that's a fair point and I thank you for that clarification. And you'd agree with me, wouldn't you, that this document is saying -- it appears to reflect that indeed that is the direction that there is this transition that is occurring as you've described it, and yet the author of this document says there are currently numerous difficulties in that regard. So you'd agree with me that this seems to indicate that that transition has not yet occurred or at least not effectively; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: One could perhaps say it's on the cusp of occurring. I mean, are now being directly organised is part of the language used in the document. But, yes, it is of course also accurate as the author of this document remarks that there were numerous difficulties encountered in that regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: There's also a reference here to the Tovarnik village police station being set up which performs all the duties and responsibilities of a police station stipulated by the laws of the Republic of Serbia. The police station was established by the MUP of Serbia. Again, any surprise there that the government of Serbia or at least organs of Serbia are involved in setting up these institutions?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't find that surprising at all, again for reasons that I've explained previously. Nor is it surprising that it would be performing at least in the interim according to the laws of the Republic of Serbia. As we know, the -- even the district in its construction and in its own evolution during 1991, the Grand National Assembly, the Serb National Council, et cetera, took a very favourable view of relevant Serbian legislation, asked that it be applied in the area of Eastern Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem, and this is hardly an area that would have been likely to have evoked disagreement between the persons running that police station and the district authorities at a later point.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And it says in the next sentence that it, namely the police station in Tovarnik, belongs to the Vukovar SUP, Erdut MUP, and it covers the territory which includes and then a number of villages are listed. Have you ever seen the nomenclature Erdut MUP or have you seen it in other documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sorry, it would be helpful for the Bench if page 3 is displayed because it's not currently displayed on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: May I also have the relevant B/C/S page displayed? Thank you. That is indeed a fascinating what I can only call an anomaly, because I do not recall seeing other documents that used the term Erdut MUP. They usually referrer to the training centre at Erdut and not to a Ministry of Internal Affairs existing at Erdut. And besides the aforementioned training centre, I have no knowledge that a Ministry of Internal Affairs was at any point established by anyone in Erdut. One can only speculate that this is again indicative of the confusion that obtains in this area during this period.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: We would tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
