utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit D21. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Could we have 06045 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could I have 06045, which is Prosecution tab 344.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: For the record, 06045 has been admitted as P378, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Now this is from the military command of the town of Ilok, and its authorship is not clear, and it has been sent to the command of the 1st Proletarian Guards Mechanised Division. And I'm interested in item 3, which is over on page 2 of the English: "A police station has been established in Ilok and one of its squads has been detached and posted to the village of Lovas formed by the MUP of Serbia and is now under the authority of SAO SBWS. In carrying out its tasks, the police station is subordinated to the command of the town of Ilok." Now, what do you make of this distinction? On the one hand it seems to say that the police station is in some sense under the authority of the district of SBWS, but then the very next sentence says that in carrying out its tasks, the police station is subordinated to the command of the town of Ilok.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we agree, as I understand it, that this is a transitional phase in this particular area of the former Yugoslavia, and we also, I believe, agree that this transition involves first the gradual establishment of civilian authorities which we agree includes the police and that that is something desired by the military that wishes to extricate itself from policing and other civilian obligations and that ultimately although many of these police organs are formed at the local level, eventually they come under the authority of first the SAO Baranja, Slavonia, and Western Srem and later the RSK. Again, we can all read the document. I can only again speculate that at this -- if we call this a snapshot in time, what we have here is a decision stating -- well, we have this police station and some units that pertain to it, and that squad or the police station is now under the authority of the SAO, but since we know that there's some unresolved issues over there which the military is still responsibility for, it's temporarily resubordinated to the military. Again that's speculation, but I think that's as far as we're going to get with that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, the point I'm getting at, sir, is would you agree with me that there appears to be different species of authority and evidence here and that one can't simply draw the inference when one sees the word authority in respect of a particular institution that that reflects an obedience to orders being issued from above? In this case we have the word authority being used to explain the relationship between the police station and the SBWS government while at the same time we have a very explicit description of a subordinate relationship in activities between that police station and the JNA town command?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would rather have preferred the word jurisdiction rather than authority in translating the B/C/S term had I had been citing this in my report. Again, it was not available when I wrote my report. But again, I mean, this is a recurring phenomenon to some extent that even long after the RSK, for that matter, is established, there are times at which police units that are under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Internal Affairs which is in turn part of the government which is in turn part of -- in turn part of the RSK or resubordinated, to me again it's a snapshot in time. This shows that what we are moving toward is the establishment of district authority and jurisdiction over the police, but we certainly haven't quite gotten there yet, and for the time being for this particular place, this particular time, this particular action, the -- and it's very clear in carrying out tasks the police station is subordinated to the command of the city of Ilok. So this is, as I understand it, for a specific set of task.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I don't believe we're very far apart on this point, but I want to try to explain what I mean in posing the question and put to you what I think the position is. I would suggest to you that one of the issues that was up in the air at this time is what is the geographic scope of the municipalities that comprise the SBWS, and it was up to various organs of the SBWS, namely the -- primarily the Assembly, to determine the scope of the geographic jurisdiction of the SBWS, and therefore it makes perfect sense to on the one hand say this police station at this location is under the authority of the SAO SBWS. In that sense it's within the jurisdictional, the geographic remit, of the SBWS, while at the same time perfectly coherently saying this police station is subordinated in its activities to the JNA which has effective control on the ground. Would you agree with me that that's -- well, I should just ask you what's your comment on that proposition?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my comment on that proposition is that as you say I don't think we're very far apart, and actually I'm not sure how we are apart on -- we're using different sets of words to describe something that is quite similar.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Thank you. And in fact, if we go to the very end of the document, significantly the author seems to believe that at that point there are no civilian authorities in existence; correct? Let me specify that question. There are no civilian authorities in existence in Ilok.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is a question how far you can push this one individual document. I would state that in the last sentence of -- or the long sentence that is the last paragraph, what they're sayings as we can see is that they will be required as soon as possible to carry out a concrete analysis and on that basis to consider and commence establishing civilian authorities. You could certainly argue from an analytical point of view that if they are only commencing the establishment of civilian authorities then there are little if any such civilian authorities present at that point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Would it shed any light, would your analysis be in any way affected if I were to tell you that there are witness statements that indicate that the JNA was prohibiting, blocking officials from the district government of the SBWS from entering Ilok at this time?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, then we confront the epistemological conundrum of what I do with that information as an analyst. I can only say that if such information is available from witnesses, then I hope that the Court will have the opportunity to hear them if they have not already done so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Could we have P369, please, which is Prosecution tab 347. This is from the 1st Guards Mechanised Division command to the 1st Military Distinct, and I would just like to interrupt myself here to make a correction in respect of the last document, which is P378, the authorship actually is clear. It's commander Milan Belic, and that's important, because we will be coming back to other documents authored by that individual. Now, coming back to P369, this is a report from the 1st Guards Mechanised Division to the 1st Military District command, and we have some discussion here about individuals who are former HDZ activists and armed forces members who have left leaving their parents and wives there. In many settlements in respect of members of the armed forces who have returned, and this is a quote: "The Serbian population through the local TO staffs is exercising pressure to have the population move out completely. On the other hand there have been many requests for the settling of Serbs from Vukovar and other Serbian areas. The pressure is particularly high in Ilok." Now, would you agree with me that at least as a point of departure we see that the 1st Guards Brigade -- excuse me, the 1st Guards Division, which is above the brigade, is taking up this issue of potential harassment in order to induce Croats to leave?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We addressed this very document yesterday, and I know that it's marked for identification because of the missing header in the translation, but, yes, this is one of the many documents in which various organs of the military are confronting this issue of the forcible removal of Croats from this area, and they are writing to their superiors in the military hierarchy to figure out what to do about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And the very -- the closing paragraph of the document says, and these are in the nature of inquiries to the higher command question: "How to guarantee the safety of the above categories and while our town commands are here on the territory, particularly when one day these affairs will be taken over by civil authorities." Would you agree with me that that's a clear indication that at that point the town command considers that it is charged with this issue and not yet the civil authorities?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Could we have P370, please. Could we have P370, please, which is Prosecution tab 348. Now, you testified about this document yesterday, and this was the document that provoked your response that there was a highly contingent relationship or that the nature of the relationship in various places between the authority of the JNA and the authority -- other authority was highly contingent. Does that imply that it was primarily local personalities who were driving the nature of that relationship between the JNA and civilian authority.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is certainly part of the reason why I used the term "contingent" in the sense that we have to look at what particular place at what particular point in time we were talking about when we make any observations not only about the nature of authority and jurisdictions but also in particular, since this is the issue we have in front of us, what the attitude was of those various organs, police, military, civilian, towards the issue of expulsion of Croats and other persons not of Serbian ethnicity. I think it's important to note that a lot of people on the local level such as the indication in the totality of documents that I've been able to examine, took inspiration or hints or signals from pronouncements made, you know, in the media and by some civilian leaders as well, both -- at all levels, especially in light of the fact that a considerable number of people were during this period propagating the view that continued co-existence between Serbs and others was impossible. If you have media or responsible officials making those kinds of statements that is obviously going to have an effect on the type of issues we have in front of us here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: We will certainly be covering those signals, but for the moment could we turn to page 2 of this document in English. And the issue primarily is about the letting of abandoned houses. So this isn't primarily addressing the question of how to curb pressure on Croatian civilians. This is the issue of abandonment and -- sorry, abandoned houses and who should move into them. Do you agree with that in the first instance?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document deals with -- with both phenomena. I mean, at least the beginning of the document, the very first question is: "How are we supposed to behave towards residents of Croat nationality who were loyal and who have not had anybody, that is had no relatives in the Croat armed forces. So there's the abandoned houses as we discussed yesterday. There's the houses in which persons of Croat and other ethnicities are still settled. It is a whole pallet of problems that are being addressed in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But you'd agree those are -- those aren't intrinsically linked issues, are they?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I certainly think that they are intrinsically linked in the sense of the fact that both abandonment of houses and later forcible removal are stemming from the presence of inter-ethnic armed conflict in this region.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Perhaps I could specify my question. The notion that there should be settlement of abandoned houses does not necessarily imply, does it, that there should be expulsion of any particular category of Croat civilians; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct strictly speaking. You could absolutely treat the settlement of abandoned houses and make very sure that no settled houses would be -- that no one would be evicted from settled houses. Again, however, that, unfortunately, was not the case here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: When you say "not the case here," are you making some reference to this document?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm making a reference to the fact that both issues are relevant here and I do not think it is coincidence that both issues are addressed in this and other documents which again deal with both abandoned houses and the question of possible evictions from settled houses in the same document and on the ground it certainly seems the case that the two issues were linked not least because some of these persons who arrived from Western Slavonia according to the documents, according to the military, TO, and other sources were not particularly interested -- let's say were not particularly patient in waiting to find out whether houses were occupied or not before settling in them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, it's the 23rd of December 1991. There appear to be a large number of refugees from Western Slavonia whose houses have -- they've been either been evicted from their houses or their houses have been destroyed. It's cold. And there appear to be vacant houses, at least according to the author of this report. Now, would you -- I would assume that you would not adopt the view under those circumstances that having a frank discussion and adopting a policy about what to do with those vacant houses necessarily implies anything at all about expulsing civilians.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, it's easy to -- to sit here and say that one could calmly, rationally discuss that one topic and not discuss the other one. The fact that both topics are, as it were, co-discussed in a number of documents, including this one, that is you have a series of questions, one series of questions pertains to, What are we going to do about abandoned houses. Another series of questions pertains to, What are we going to do with the pressure to remove people forcibly from homes in which they reside, that to me makes it clear that you cannot other than purely academically and abstractly separate these two discussions. And you're absolutely right that these repeated documents make it clear, and we know that large numbers of refugees, Serb refugees in particular, had been forcibly expelled from Western Slavonia. As you say, it's cold. They're arriving. They're clearly not the most patient of people. That's quite understandable. But this is -- and again a very unfortunate aspect of where we get a spiral of regrettable acts which we can say where did it start, that is a good question, but it's certainly continuing here now with the arrival from Western Slavonia of these people in Eastern Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: But surely you wouldn't say that the only way to avoid becoming implicitly involved in expulsing -- expelling would be a better word. Expelling residents is to simply adopt a policy saying no vacant houses can be settled regardless of the circumstances. You wouldn't adopt that view, would you?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You will perhaps recall that I referred yesterday to military documents from the same period where they expressed their displeasure with the fact that people were being permitted to move immediately into houses without being given any written documentation, that there was nothing regulating that process, and so at least on the part of some representatives of the military, they were very much hoping that notwithstanding the exigencies that we have just discussed, and I think we agree about of those circumstances there, it would have been highly desirable to have at least attempted to implement some process so that those people who needed to be settled post-haste in abandoned houses could do so in a proper manner. And I think from -- again from the totality of the documentation that that is implicitly linked to the concern that those same military representatives express that in the absence of such procedures, there was an atmosphere in which people were being forcibly evicted, and for those reasons I cannot accept and would not agree with a characterisation of those two issues as being completely separate.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, in fact what you seem to be saying is that it was vital that proper procedures be adopted to avoid improper conduct and expulsions. Isn't that what you're saying? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is precisely what the military representatives are saying. And if we look at the document in front of us, in the second to last paragraph they are saying -- they're reminding themselves and others that they need to take care of public law and order, of security, and of citizens regardless of ethnicity, and that they are not allowed -- they cannot permit themselves to allow any harassment or mistreatment of citizens. So again given the other reports we have, what we know about what types of incidents of mistreatment and harassment were ongoing, the military is, as you say, of the opinion that it would be highly desirable to adopt proper procedures for the regulation of settlement into abandoned houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And one final question: And you're saying that that was vital to maintaining law and order - correct? - at least in the perception of those JNA officers?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN AXBOE NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I'm saying is that they expressed that this would be highly desirable. I would also note that in one of the documents we viewed yesterday, they expressed concern that some of the arriving families from Western Slavonia were not taking -- one household arriving from Western Slavonia was not taking just one abandoned house but was in fact taking several abandoned houses. So they again wanted to establish a procedure as I see it from the military's perspective at least among some of them their -- their hopes were that the establishment of such procedures could slow down if not eliminate illegal expulsions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Dr. Nielsen, thank you very much. I'd like to keep you here for a couple of more hours, but I don't think anyone else would be happy about that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wouldn't mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Dr. Nielsen. Unfortunately, that is not possible, and you'll have to return at some point in time to finish cross and re-examination. In the meantime, I remind you that you are still under oath and that the normal procedures apply about discussing your testimony with other people and talking to one of the parties. Except for the fact that we all agreed that for planning purposes, you could be contacted by the parties in the presence of or with the help of victim and witness section of the Tribunal. So for the moment, your testimony is delayed until further notice. You will be escorted out, and I thank you very much and wish you a safe journey home, if that's where you're going.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, via Berlin. Thank you very much, Your Honour. Thank you for your clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I know we've passed the time but very briefly. I was reminded that the video that I had played yesterday, the one in Bijeljina with Ms. Plavsic and Goran Hadzic, has not been tender after I asked the question this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: That was 65 ter 4826.1. I'd like to submit it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit P381. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, earlier today Your Honour asked for the Prosecution position in respect of the Defence motion to replace the translation of Exhibit D5. It was filed the day before yesterday, and I've been looking into this this morning, but we weren't aware -- I don't know if the Trial Chamber considers it to be urgent, but I wonder if the Trial Chamber would have a problem with our filing a written response on Monday. I would like to look into it just quickly and consult a bit which I've not been able to do fully while in court today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I don't think that will be a problem, Mr. Stringer. Thank you. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 21st day of January, 2013, at 9.00 a.m.
